prompt: An NVMe SSD on PCIe 4.0 x4 vastly outperforms a SATA III SSD. Concretely, which two factors combine to cause this?
choices: Wider/faster PCIe lanes (multiple ~2 GB/s lanes vs. SATA's single ~0.55 GB/s link) plus NVMe's massively deeper, more parallel command queues vs. AHCI's single 32-deep queue
NVMe SSDs simply use faster NAND flash chips than SATA SSDs
PCIe eliminates the need for a command protocol entirely, removing all overhead
SATA is limited only by cable length, not by its electrical line rate

prompt: What most fundamentally distinguishes USB from PCIe as a bus architecture?
